Competing contractors operate in a Bangalore neighbourhood. Each is trying to supply power and water to as many houses as possible, without much concern for how their actions affect the others. Meanwhile, roads are constantly dug up for Metro work, VIP visits, and floods, wreaking havoc on the infrastructure. The city's residents are left to deal with unpredictable power and water, and must suffer in silence.

Swalpa adjust maadi

A game of pipes and dug-up roads!

Players: 2-4  •  Rounds: 36  •  Time per game: 30 mins

Components

A game board
Cards: PARK, ROADWORKS, PIPE
Tokens: SITE, HOUSE, POWER/WATER, GUARD

Objective

Players are contractors laying power and water pipes on a board. A contractor who connects both resources to a square claims a house on that square. One contractor's work can disconnect another's pipes, so houses have tanks to store power and water. A house stays standing only as long as neither of its tanks go empty, and players only survive as long as they have houses on the board. You must knock out every rival to win.

The Board

The board is a square grid. It comes set up with a fixed set of PARK squares, a set of PIPE cards on all other squares, and two HOUSE tokens each for players 1 to 4. If you are playing with fewer than four players, ignore the extra houses. Each player has a score box below the board, tracking their current number of houses.

The board at the start of a game, with parks, pipes, sites, and houses.

The Deck

Each player is dealt a fixed deck of 36 PIPE cards, and plays one card per round over the 36 rounds of the game. The total number of remaining cards of each type is indicated by dots above the card. Once a card type is depleted from a deck, it is greyed out and can no longer be played.

The deck showing card quantities.

Playing a Round

Each player must choose a square, remove its existing card, and replace it with a fresh card. But their choices are made in secret, leading to collisions!

At the start of each round each player secretly chooses a PIPE card from their own deck and a square on the board. All players then reveal their choices at once. Each player's choice is recorded serially, and then all players' moves are replayed together. In 1-player mode Player 1 is the human, Player 2 is the computer. The Auto button autoplays your move. Computer play, Autoplay, and Replay are indicated by a PLAY icon in the score box.

Each player removes the existing card from their chosen square and replaces it with the card from their deck. They also move their GUARD token on their chosen space, to indicate their most recent turn. You can try up to five choices; your chosen card and chosen square are highlighted by an orange border; tap the chosen square again to confirm your move; that square is then guarded, indicated by grey shading.

1. Choose a card
2. Choose a square
3. Confirm your move

Choosing a card, choosing a square, and confirming your move.

If two or more players choose the same square, this is a COLLISION! Their cards are discarded, and a ROADWORKS card is placed on that square. The square is left unguarded, and players can choose it on subsequent turns. Each player involved in a COLLISION also collects a single COLLISION POINT (red dots in the player's score box). These COLLISION POINTS are valuable (see 'Collision Champions!').

A collision!
Houses built and removed

Once all cards have been played, power and water flows are updated across the board (see 'Power and Water Supplies'). New houses are built, house power and water tanks are updated, and houses with empty tanks are removed (see 'Building and Removing Houses'). Newly-built houses and newly-removed houses are highlighted with +1 and -1 at the end of the round.

Off-limits squares: No card may be played on a PARK square, or on any square with a GUARD token. A player cannot play a card on a square that has another player's HOUSE. Trying to play on an off-limits square will trigger a message that explains why this can't be done.

Power and Water Supplies

The board's top and bottom edges SUPPLY POWER, shown in dark red, and its left and right edges SUPPLY WATER, shown in dark blue. The main goal of the game is to bring these resources INTO the board by placing PIPE cards cleverly.

Each PIPE card has a single POWER pipe, initially light red, and a single WATER pipe, initially light blue, crossing it. Each edge of a PIPE card has a single pipe ending on it.

When a PIPE card is placed next to a SUPPLY edge, the resource will only CONNECT to the card if both the SUPPLY and the PIPE are of the SAME COLOUR. For example, if a blue pipe touches the red supply edge, the colours are mismatched and power WILL NOT flow into the water pipe.

If a POWER pipe on a square is connected to a POWER SUPPLY, it changes from light to dark red. This pipe can then supply power to another square, as long as it connects to a POWER pipe on that square. Similarly, if a WATER pipe on a square is connected to a WATER SUPPLY, it changes from light to dark blue. This pipe can then supply water to another square, as long as it connects to a WATER pipe on that square. Power and water flows on a square are determined independently.

Before
After

Long power and water pipes are initially unconnected to their respective supplies. Two PIPE cards are placed on the board that connect these pipes to the POWER SUPPLY and WATER SUPPLY, so the pipes change from light to dark.

Building and Removing Houses

A square whose neighbours already supply it with both power and water but has no house is marked with a SITE token (dark brown shading). Houses and sites cannot form on the outermost layer of the board.

Power and water will not necessarily flow INTO the site, that requires that the pipes on that square actually match the supplies on its edges. If a card is played on a site that allows it to connect to both power and water, a house is built on that site. This house is claimed by the player who placed the card. The SITE token is removed and replaced by a HOUSE token in the player's colour (the brown colour goes away, and replaced with a house icon shown with the roof in the correct player's colour).

A house forms when the card played on a site connects it to both power and water.

Each house has two tanks, one for power and one for water, each with a capacity of three units. This is indicated by placing POWER or WATER tokens on the square (red and blue battery-type indicators).

Power and water tanks being depleted.

At the end of every round, every house on the board is checked. If the house is still connected to power/water, then its power/water tank rises by one unit. If it is not connected to power/water, then its power/water tank falls by one unit. If either tank reaches zero, the house is removed before the next round begins.

Water down to its last unit
Removed next round

A house loses its final unit of water, and is removed from the board.

Winning the Game

Knockout. A player is eliminated the instant they have no houses left standing at the end of a round. The last player with any houses remaining wins. If every remaining player loses their last house in the same round, the game ends in a draw. If the game completes 36 rounds with two or more players still standing, it also ends in a draw.

Collision Champion! If a player collects seven COLLISION POINTS they win immediately, and the game ends. If more than one player reaches seven COLLISION POINTS in the same round, they all win together.

Happy digging!
